_readme: The points pool. Every bullet you could ever put on a CV lives here exactly once.
id          stable slug, never reuse
roleId      which role in profile.json this bullet sits under
text        the default wording
variants    same underlying fact, re-angled for a different audience.
NEVER put a new claim in a variant - only a rewording.
tags        from profile/taxonomy.json - this drives JD matching
strength    1-5, your own view of how impressive it is. Ties break on this.
status      active | draft | retired
inMaster    true if it appears on the 2026 master CV
Keep every number here defensible in an interview.

2026-10-30 date correction from Parag: Nutanix Member of Technical Staff began July 2022; the move to Team Lead was July 2024; Nutanix employment ended December 2025. The Team Lead period is July 2024-December 2025, superseding older notes here and in xyz-review.json that say 2024-2026. See profile/profile.json formDates for portal month values.

2026-10-27 behavioural interview evidence: Parag confirmed the government-customer VM migration escalation occurred during his Nutanix Team Lead role and that the customer's failure rate fell from 10% to around 1%. This supersedes his initial 4-5% baseline recollection. Captured as nutanix-government-migration-recovery, separate from the banking migration. Migration volume remains uncertain; use thousands of VMs per weekend. See profile/xyz-review.json profileClarifications for actions and evidence limits.

2026-10-27 HUD interview preparation: At Nutanix, product managers supplied priorities and Parag worked with programme managers to execute them. He particularly enjoyed delivery: working with different stakeholders, determining what needed to happen and when, and following the work through to delivery. This confirms his motivation for Technical Program Manager over Product Manager; no formal programme-manager title, specific programme outcome or additional delivery metric is established. See profile/xyz-review.json profileClarifications.

2026-10-25 HUD follow-up: Parag is working on course-specific MBA agents, each with the context of a course's shared material and teaching, so he can apply frameworks to real situations (example: negotiation preparation using Horacio Falcao's teaching). Completion, tools, demonstrability and measured results are unspecified. This is a personal learning project, not an employment achievement. He also confirmed 30% delivered operations cost savings at Valeo from insights based on mapping ten months of UAE appointment data and analysing staffing capacity, schedules and locations; this supersedes the prior forecast-only wording of valeo-cost-strategy. Savings baseline, measurement period and overlap with route-app savings remain unspecified.

2026-10-25 conversation evidence, HUD email: Parag's personal daily-life assistant project includes MediaBot, CookBot (help deciding what to cook), ShoppingBot (help shopping for things) and TravelBot (help deciding travel plans). He is also working on automating the end-to-end job-search pipeline while aiming to minimise token consumption. These are personal projects in progress; no completed end-to-end deployment, specific implementation tools, measured token savings or reliability results were confirmed. See profile/xyz-review.json profileClarifications; do not invent an employment role or achievement metric.

2026-10-19 conversation evidence: Parag's supplied Maxify application email describes an in-progress personal life-automation ecosystem, including MediaBot and CookBot, with asynchronous tasks, decision logic and persistent state management. Employer, completion, deployment, users and measured impact are not established; do not assign it to an employment role or claim shipped production agents. The source wording is currently architecting, not a completed delivery achievement. See profile/xyz-review.json profileClarifications.

Mobility confirmed 2026-10-19 for the Sheffield Management Associate application: Parag is willing to relocate internationally after the programme. This is a preference, not an achievement or confirmation of work authorisation.

CV layout preference confirmed 2026-10-15: aim for at least 50% width on each experience bullet's final line. Shorten orphan endings or expand them with useful supported detail; measure actual wrapping with tools/cv-builder/lib/metrics.js.
XYZ review, 2026-10-15: profile/xyz-review.json records the assessment and missing evidence for every point.
Pre-review recovery copy: archive/data-backups/points.before-xyz-2026-10-15.json. IDs and variant labels were preserved.
New confirmations: 20% fewer bugs (replaces 30% code quality); one year to Eleven01 ICO; Valeo saves 20,000 km and AED 12,200 monthly.
Release cadence and promotions are separate points: testing resources enabled the release increase; feedback, clear goals and leadership visibility supported promotions.

2026-10-28 portfolio summary: added amantya-verizon-tower-analytics (stated by Parag in chat) and cognizant-mesh-library, cognizant-trendsetter, touchnote-api-performance, eleven01-spokesperson (from his LinkedIn PDF). No existing point changed. Open conflicts NOT applied, awaiting Parag: amantya-ios-retail (bank: footfall and sales +10%; chat 2026-10-28: revenue +about 30%); iitj-ignus (bank: $10K; LinkedIn: INR 1M); role dates/titles in profile.json vs LinkedIn (EverHaus Jan-May vs Feb-Jun 2026; Eleven01 2019 vs Sep 2018 start; Touchnote 'Backend Developer' vs 'Senior Backend developer'). LinkedIn's 'code quality 30%' is superseded by nutanix-code-standards (20% fewer bugs) and LinkedIn places the custodian-bank migration under MTS although the bank records Team Lead (confirmed 2026-10-22).

2026-10-28 conflicts resolved by Parag: amantya-ios-retail now 'revenue about 20%'; iitj-ignus $10K = INR 1M (same figure); Touchnote title changed to 'Senior Backend Developer' in profile.json. Still open: EverHaus and Eleven01 dates vs LinkedIn.

2026-10-28 LinkedIn vs CV, decided by Parag: the EverHaus and Eleven01 date differences are accepted (LinkedIn keeps Feb-Jun 2026 and Sep 2018-Feb 2020; CV and profile.json unchanged). The Valeo CEO agreed to the LinkedIn title 'Product Manager Intern'; the CV and profile.json keep 'Management Intern'. These are no longer open conflicts.

2026-11-06: Parag gave the levels for the three Nutanix promotions and 0% attrition; added to nutanix-engineer-promotions notes and a retention-forward variant. Attrition period and team size still unconfirmed.

Earlier notes: separate from valeo-cost-strategy (30%); do not add savings together. 2026-10-25 HUD email context about a route-optimisation model remains unverified.

points.text: Reduced 400+ critical security risks to 20 and 500+ licensing risks to zero on Nutanix Move through technical diligence and remediation with Legal and Compliance

variants.label: short
variants.text: Reduced 400+ critical security risks to 20 and 500+ licensing risks to zero through technical diligence on Nutanix Move

variants.label: risk-forward
variants.text: Reduced Nutanix Move's critical security risks from 400+ to 20 and licensing risks from 500+ to zero by owning diligence and remediation with Legal and Compliance

points.notes: Added 2026-09-04 from Parag. The single most valuable point in the pool for technology-diligence roles — it is a real technical due diligence with quantified findings and a remediation outcome, carrying the “research” tag whose taxonomy keywords include “due diligence”. Supersedes nutanix-code-standards on the engineering-quality axis; do not run both unless the page is roomy. ROLE CONFIRMED 2026-10-22: Parag confirmed this was during the Team Lead period (2024-2026). Numbers are his: 400+ critical security risks and 500+ licence risks, reduced to 20 and 0 respectively. 2026-09-04, wording chosen by Parag: default is now the "Owned ... worked with Legal and Compliance" phrasing, which pairs each risk count with its own outcome (400+ -> 20, 500+ -> 0) instead of collapsing them into "20 and zero". Names the product as Nutanix Move rather than "the Move migration product". The short variant is the 1-line fallback and knowingly drops the word "critical" and the Legal/Compliance partnership - use it only when the page is genuinely tight, because 400 CRITICAL findings is a materially stronger claim than 400 findings. Deliberately no percentage framing: 95%/100% would be derived from figures that are themselves approximate (400+, 500+).

Nutanix Move feature that moves workloads from VMware to Nutanix by changing the underlying hypervisor of the hardware while workloads are live in production. Parag owned discovery, requirements, architecture decisions, the team and final delivery. Four teams built it (his plus three others); coordinating them was a main challenge. Technical crux: any issue must stop the process and recover gracefully - no bad recovery. Started December 2024, shipped September 2025 (about nine months; Parag first said 'one year'). Base: about 2,000 customers running VMware on Nutanix (mixed stack), at risk of churn; about 1,000 enterprise customers moved to the Nutanix platform using it (confirmed 2026-11-01). Do NOT say 'retained' or 'prevented churn': whether they would otherwise have left is not established. UNCONFIRMED: period over which the ~1,000 was counted, exact feature name in the product, whether the 20,000-workload banking migration used it (keep nutanix-banking-migration separate). 'Moved ... customers' means customers migrated using the feature. Collides with nutanix-team-budget (same team) - fine together, but avoid also running nutanix-files-migration's 'leading development' framing as a second ownership story.

points.text: Helped reduce a government customer's VM migration failure rate from 10% to around 1% by grouping boot failures by cause, prioritising the largest categories and coordinating fixes with the team
points.notes: Confirmed by Parag on 2026-10-27 during behavioural interview preparation. Employer and role confirmed as Nutanix Team Lead. Customer migrated thousands of VMs per weekend; initial recollection of 2,000 was revised uncertainly to 3,000 or 4,000, so retain approximate wording. Latest confirmed baseline of 10% supersedes the initial 4-5% estimate; final failure rate was around 1%. Do not convert approximate figures into a precise relative improvement or infer absolute VM counts. The problem had persisted for about a month before reaching the team late in the cycle. Parag grouped failures by cause (including script timeouts and VM configuration differences) and prioritised the largest categories. The team's first release did not resolve the reported issue; another fix followed. The overall outcome is confirmed, but the exact release responsible and measurement period are not. Parag personally handled some tense customer calls without teammates present, kept a calm tone, and returned to the team to discuss next steps so engineers could focus on investigation. Do not infer sole coding ownership, full migration completion, customer satisfaction, or a demonstrated change in delegation or openness to alternatives. Keep the government customer anonymous and separate from nutanix-banking-migration.
